heading: Jeopardy teams
items: Teams are mixed. Boys and girls compete together.
A team is **7 youth minimum, 10 maximum**.
More than 16 youth registered means you may form a second team. **Two teams per church is the limit.**
With two teams, your church's final score is the average of both.
Substitutions happen between games, never during one.

heading: Hymns
items: Middle school and high school perform the hymn **live**, with everyone attending.
If fewer than **70% of your registered youth** perform, your church drops one rank.
Elementary may split a grade group once. Both scores are averaged.
Recording groups cap at **25 children**. Over 30, split into two groups and record every required hymn with each.
3rd and 4th grade may record Golgotha in sections.
KG may record English and Coptic separately.

heading: Exams
items: Online exams open Jul 18 and close automatically **Jul 26 at 11:59 PM**.
KG and PreK take Bible, memorization, and Coptic on **paper**. Print them, have your servants grade them, then enter scores in the shared sheet.
The Coptic exam is taken individually near the end of each Jeopardy day.
Travelling? Ask Abouna privately to open a specific exam for your church.

heading: Sports
items: **No volleyball for MS and HS boys this year** — too few days available and very low turnout last year.
Ping pong is a church team competition. Send 3 per tournament: 3rd–4th (2 boys, 1 girl), 5th–6th boys, 5th–6th girls, 7th–8th boys, 7th–8th girls, HS boys, HS girls.
At sports events, **only servants and playing youth may attend**. Anyone else will be asked to leave.
Verify every name with the youth before sending a roster. Don't send names straight off the sign-up sheet.

heading: Hosting and reimbursement
items: The hosting church provides a light meal for guests — a sandwich, a snack, a drink.
Send receipts for food and equipment privately to Fr Akhnoukh at St. Meena for reimbursement.
Bring last year's trophy back. Trophies are reused, not reordered each year.
Keep an adequate servant-to-youth ratio for the whole event.
